title.narrative: International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) + Beyond Oil and Gas Alliance (BOGA)

description.narrative: Major global economies more systematically shift public financial flows in ways that significantly accelerate the transition away from fossil fuels toward clean energy, while promoting improved social welfare and overall sustainable economic development.

tag.narrative: By 2030, increase substantially the share of renewable energy in the global energy mix

title.narrative: 2.2 Efficient pricing and energy/carbon tax reform undertaken in at least 1 jurisdiction.
Fossil fuel taxation increased in at least 1 jurisdiction arising from a contribution by the project and leading to more efficient pricing.

target.value: Opportunities for fossil fuel taxation increase reviewed and a few candidate jurisdictions selected.

actual.value: Complete. At the national level, candidate taxes which could be increased have been identified. More generally, IISD-GSI is promoting that transport taxation and taxes on coal production are a generic option for raising finance for recovery.

target.value: Planned promotion activities for fossil fuel taxation increase completed in a selected jurisdiction.

actual.value: Complete. Indonesia announced its intention to introduce a carbon tax on coal from mid-2022, although implementation has been delayed due to record high coal prices.

target.value: Fossil fuel taxation increased in the selected jurisdiction.

actual.value: Completed as per 2022

target.value: Planned promotion activities for fossil fuel taxation increase completed in the selected jurisdiction.

actual.value: Year 4 target already complete. In 2022, India imposed a windfall profits tax on oil producing and refining companies that were benefiting from high international oil prices, following the Ukraine-Russia war. Although the taxes were adjusted several times, IISD-GSI estimated that the windfall tax raised revenues ranging from US$ 40-53 billion in FY23. India also announces intentions to establish a national carbon market.

title.narrative: 1.3 Non-government actors at international and at national levels, including CSOs and the private sector, take part in efforts to enable sustainable subsidy reforms.

The number of statements, agreements, events, formal coalitions or other joint public-facing activity from more than one institution in target countries (where there is evidence of an escalation of these types of activities that consolidate and build on each other in each target country).

target.value: At least one additional statement/ agreement/ event/ formal coalition/or other joint public-facing activity from more than one institution in 3 target countries (that consolidates and/or advances earlier activities).

actual.value: Complete. At the UNFCCC COP27, IISD-GSI organized and/or co-organized multiple events with multiple partners (including Friends of FFSR, OECD, UNEP, UNDP, etc), including CSO participation from both the global south and north to promote fossil fuel subsidy reform.

target.value: At least one additional statement/ agreement/ event/ formal coalition/or other joint public-facing activity from more than one institution in 3 target countries.

actual.value: Complete. IISD-GSI continues to work closely with, and expand, our network of CSOs in our 3 focus countries and in others (for example Nigeria). A large number of Events and other joint public-facing activities have been held.

target.value: At least one additional statement/ agreement/ event/ formal coalition/ or other joint public-facing activity from more than one institution in 3 target countries (that consolidates and/or advances earlier activities).

At least one additional statement/ agreement/ event/ formal coalition/or other joint public-facing activity from more than one institution in 3 target countries (that consolidates and/or advances earlier activities).

actual.value: Ongoing. IISD has held several events (virtual due to COVID-19) in Indonesia working closely with CSO partners. In South Africa, IISD has collaborated closely on inventory work with leading economic CSOs including TIPS and Meridian Economics. Indian collaboration has been ongoing with CEEW (a CSO with strong links to government) and the signing of a formal MoU with the government’s internal think tank, Niti Aayog, is part of an ongoing discussion.

title.narrative: 1.2 Policy-makers in target countries being (better) able to prepare and plan reform policies.
Policy-makers in target countries are making use of GSI assistance (in an escalation from awareness to implementation).

target.value: Policy-makers in at least 3 target countries are using GSI material to increase awareness of key gaps in preparedness for reform.

actual.value: Complete. IISD-GSI has strong links and relationships with parts of the Indian and Indonesian government, who have both used and requested IISD-GSI materials. Materials were also used by Nigeria, Guinea and Canada during the year 2020.

target.value: Policy-makers in at least 3 target countries are aware of material produced by GSI, which is of relevance to gaps in their own preparedness.

actual.value: Complete. Policymakers have spoken at several IISD events, provided feedback and welcomed IISD research. For example, in India, the CEO of the government's think tank, Niti Aayog, wrote a foreword for the publication, saying “Such work is critical to encourage thinking and accountability across India’s many energy institutions and policies. It is commended that the underlying data, definitions and methodology are all fully transparent, enabling all policy professionals to draw on them.“ In Indonesia, officials publicly noted the importance of IISD’s work on FFSR, as well as the necessity of subsidy reform in the country ay IISD events. In South Africa, officials from the Treasury have peer reviewed our inventory and agreed to speak at the launch webinar of the report.

target.value: Policy-makers in at least 3 target countries are aware of the existence of country-specific knowledge and policy options produced by GSI or local partners, which can be used to address gaps in preparedness for reform.

actual.value: Complete. Related to subsidies efforts was positive progress in 2022 on the Glasgow Statement on International Public Support for the Clean Energy Transition, for which Canada released policy guidelines in late 2022. In India, IISD-GSI inventory report and update were launched in partnership with CEEW and presented through multiple events attended by CSOs and government officials. In South Africa, IISD-GSI brings in national experts from TIPS and E3G to jointly launch and debate the results of a first national subsidy inventory.

target.value: Policy-makers at least 3 target countries identify necessary means to enact identified options (e.g. resources, legislative changes, implementation responsibilities) and implement necessary policies to enable their use.

title.narrative: 3.2 Swaps are promoted and advocated focusing on 3 emerging economies.
Opportunities are identified for on-grid, outside on-grid and other Swaps.

target.value: Opportunities for on-grid and outside on-grid Swaps identified in 2 countries.

actual.value: Complete. In India, IISD supports Indian policymakers at the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy through the release of a guidebook to support their flagship scheme KUSUM, that aims to install over 2 million solar irrigation pumps by 2022. This involved extensive engagement with over 40 national and sub national government officials. The work is now expanding in 2022. In Indonesia, a range of options have been developed and discussed with government officials.

target.value: Opportunities for on-grid and outside on-grid Swaps identified in 3 countries.

actual.value: Complete. In India, IISD-GSI has continued to support the flagship scheme PM KUSUM that can swap fossil-intensive electricity subsidies into solar power for agriculture and irrigation, publishing one guidebook and preparing another, including extensive engagement with state policy officials.In Indonesia, IISD-GSI has provided technical expertise to the Vice President’s Office on how to support clean cooking and LPG subsidy reform.In South Africa, IISD-GSI identifies specific opportunities to shift government support plans away from natural gas and towards building renewables, batteries and strengthening the grid, and was as tracking the first year of discussions on the Just Energy Transition Partnership (JETP), which has significant implications for domestic support policies.

target.value: Opportunities for on-grid and outside on-grid Swaps identified in 1 country.

actual.value: Complete. Specific opportunities for Swaps were identified in each of the 3 focus countries. On a generic level, the Energy Policy Tracker was used to highlight ongoing practice and potential for Swaps, in each of the 3 focus countries and for many other countries.

target.value: Opportunities for on-grid and outside on-grid Swaps are being self -identified beyond the 3 focus economies.

title.narrative: 2.1 Efficient pricing and energy/carbon tax reform promoted nationally and internationally, based on successful experience in the Nordic region and elsewhere.
Information campaign carried out based on review and evidence of successful cases leads to changed perceptions among decision makers.

target.value: Information campaign effect in changing perceptions reviewed end of year 2 and information campaign/promotion activities adjusted and carried out.

actual.value: Complete. Internationally, IISD-GSI “Boom and Bust” campaign highlights the opportunities and risks of increased reliance on fossil energy taxation among major emerging economies, and makes the case for higher tax rates in the short-term, combined with investing fossil “super revenues” into clean energy and social protection. It focuses on the emerging economies of Brazil, Russia, India, Indonesia, China and South Africa. Indonesia G20 activities include a strong messaging sub-component on swaps and fossil energy taxation. Both IISD - GSI Progress report: period January-December 2022 77 efforts achieve significant engagement through dialogues and media coverage.

target.value: Review of experience and success cases undertaken, and information campaign carried out.

actual.value: Complete. Success cases reviewed and published. Outreach efforts have started and are ongoing.

target.value: Information campaign effect in changing perceptions reviewed end of year 3 and information campaign/promotion activities adjusted and carried out.
Information campaign effect in changing perceptions reviewed end of year 1 and information campaign/promotion activities adjusted and carried out.

actual.value: In progress. A campaign for an international coal tax floor (minimum tax) has been developed and will be implemented when record-high coal prices start to decline, potentially during India’s G20 year in 2023. In South Africa, Memory Machingambi, a treasury official commented after a webinar on green taxes “thank you for the platform to talk about our work and opportunity to learn from other jurisdictions’ experiences. It was an interesting discussion indeed from which I learned and got me thinking of issues we will need to address in the review of our EFR policy paper.”

title.narrative: 1.1 International processes and organizations support the inclusion of subsidy reform in international processes and forums.

Availability of influential policy studies, international datasets and activities that serve to promote inclusion of subsidy issues in international processes, statements and forums (where there is evidence that the studies, datasets and activities consolidate and/or advance earlier information and respond to the Friends annual work plan18 in particular).

target.value: At least one additional GSI-supported influential statement, policy study or international dataset is produced as a result of international processes or fora in support of fossil-fuel subsidy reform or the need for sustainable reform (that consolidates and/or advances earlier activities).

actual.value: Complete. In September 2022, alongside the UN General Assembly meeting in New York, BOGA issued a 10-government statement calling for an acceleration in the transition away from fossil fuel dependency, and for a massive increase in energy efficiency and renewable energy investment, to deliver long-term climate and energy security. At UNFCCC COP27 in late 2022, BOGA welcomed Chile, Fiji and Washington State in the US as its newest members. In India, IISD-GSI inventory report and update were launched in partnership with CEEW.In early 2022 we released a major report about how this legislation could be implemented. For this study we examined international best practices in various jurisdictions including Spain, Germany, New Zealand, South Africa, and various U.S. states.

target.value: At least one additional GSI-supported influential statement, policy study or international dataset is produced as a result of international processes or fora in support of fossil-fuel subsidy reform or the need for sustainable reform (that consolidates and/or advances earlier activities).

actual.value: Complete. The Glasgow Pact COP26 Decision included FFS for the first time, and the WTO MC12 Statement reiterated the need for FFS Reform with extended support from WTO Members, include the EU for the first time.

target.value: At least one additional GSI-supported influential statement, policy study or international dataset is produced as a result of international processes or fora in support of fossil-fuel subsidy reform or the need for sustainable reform (that consolidates and/or advances earlier activities).

actual.value: Complete. The “Friends” 5th Anniversary of the Paris Communiqué is an example of a statement. IISD-GSI has also laid considerable groundwork on data, both with support to the SDG 12.c.1 Indicator reporting and the development of a join database of FFS with the OECD.

target.value: At least one additional GSI-supported influential statement, policy study or international dataset is produced as a result of international processes or fora in support of fossil-fuel subsidy reform or the need for sustainable reform (that consolidates and/or advances earlier activities).

title.narrative: 3.3 Environment for PSICE improved, notably for employing domestic finance in emerging economies (but also assessing opportunities for international organisations).
Investment being increased as a result of PSICE related road-blocks are identified and unblocking solutions promoted.

target.value: Road-blocks identified, analysed and brought up for discussion in 2 emerging economies leading to investment being increased in at least 2 countries.

actual.value: Complete. India selects winning firms to participate in its support schemes on solar cell and battery manufacturing. IISD-GSI is directly supporting Invest India.Engagement on South Africa’s JETP focuses on critically questioning efforts to shift support mechanisms towards natural gas, while Indonesia confirms its own JETP, opening up prospects for increased investment in clean energy.

target.value: Road-blocks identified, analysed and brought up for discussion in 3 emerging economies leading to investment being increased in at least 3 countries.
Road-blocks identified, analysed and brought up for discussion in 1 emerging economy.

actual.value: Ongoing, in all 3 focus countries. Again a particular focus on SOEs has been identified as key to understanding the roadblocks in all the 3 focus countries.

target.value: Road-blocks identified, analysed and brought up for discussion in 2 emerging economies leading to investment being increased in at least 1 country.

actual.value: Ongoing. Mechanisms have been analysed for all emerging economies. Initial discussions on their implementation have been undertaken.

title.narrative: 3.4 Increased PSICE in 3 emerging economies from public money from Swaps or other project outputs.
Mechanisms for use of public and development finance from Swaps identified and promoted.

target.value: Mechanisms for use of public and development finance from Swaps identified in 2 emerging economies leading to solutions being implemented and investment being increased in at least 1 country.

actual.value: Complete. Generic mechanisms developed for all countries. In India, IID-GSI is supporting India's most coal intensive SoEs by developing training programs for their officials to support diversifying from coal and planning around clean energy.

target.value: Mechanisms for use of public and development finance from Swaps identified in 2 emerging economies leading to solutions being implemented and investment being increased in at least 2 countries.

actual.value: Complete. IISD-GSI helps establish centre of excellence on SOE transition, including extensive training sessions for over 200 officials, and IISD-GSI publishes accompanying analysis of risks and opportunities for three of the country’s most coal-intensive SOEs (PSUs).Similar IISD - GSI Progress report: period January-December 2022 64 inventories in Indonesia and South Africa make the case for shifts in public support. In Indonesia, the government made strong political commitments to increase support for clean energy as part of securing its JETP deal on climate finance.

target.value: Mechanisms for use of public and development finance from Swaps identified in 3 emerging economies leading to solutions being implemented and investment being increased in at least 3 countries.
Mechanisms for use of public and development finance from Swaps identified in 1 emerging economy.

actual.value: Ongoing. Investigations of the specific mechanisms which would have best potential in each of the 3 focus countries underway. A particular focus on SOEs as agents, or constrainers, of transition to clean energy has been identified. Movement of recovery funds away from fossil fuels offers further potential and links.

title.narrative: 3.1 A practical taxonomy of Swaps and guidance on how they can be designed, disseminated and implemented.
The taxonomy and guidance of Swaps is developed, used and improved.

target.value: Taxonomy is developed and disseminated.

actual.value: Complete. Taxonomy is complete (published and reported in full within “Achieving a Fossil-Free Recovery” report) and the logic for shifting public support is fully embedded in all activities regarding the G20, UNFCCC and in national partner countries. See reporting on Outputs 1.1, 1.2 and 3.2 for more detail. Consultations on specific swaps opportunities continue to take place in national partner countries, including with respect to solar irrigation, electric vehicles and providing support through SOEs.

target.value: Outline taxonomy is developed and stakeholders consulted.

actual.value: Ongoing. Taxonomy is complete (published and reported in full within “Achieving a Fossil-Free Recovery” report). Stakeholder consultation incomplete.

target.value: Analytical work is developed to form the basis/foundation for a taxonomy.

actual.value: Ongoing. The taxonomy will be finalised and published in 2021. The range of potential swaps has been increased.

target.value: Updated and expanded taxonomy is developed and disseminated.

actual.value: Taxonomy is complete

title.narrative: 3. Fossil fuel subsidy Swaps and private sector investment promoted, with a focus on transition to clean energy in emerging economies.

Significantly increased understanding and uptake of mechanisms for Swaps and for using public money from Swaps to incentivise private sector investment in clean energy in participating emerging economies, including from a gender equity and poverty reduction perspective.

target.value: Advocacy has increased awareness of Swaps and the potential for private sector investment for on-grid RE in up to 3 emerging economies. There is evidence of uptake on case study/business models for off-grid solutions in up to 3 countries, and Swaps are being developed outside the main grid.

title.narrative: 1. National and international reform of fossil fuel and electricity subsidies advanced, including through the “Friends of Fossil Fuel Subsidy Reform Group”

Significant advancement in policies, coordination mechanisms, and regulatory frameworks (that have been improved with support by the project reflecting increased awareness of and action on the opportunities presented by FFSR to help meet energy and climate commitments and targets, including inclusion of FFSR in countries’ NDCs or other national targets and plans, and including from a gender equity and poverty reduction perspective).

target.value: Evidence of increased awareness of the opportunity presented by FFSR to help meet energy and climate commitments and targeted adoption of at least 2 policy, regulatory or coordination measures in each of the partner countries. Analytical piece outlining the role of subsidies and financing for fossil fuels and justifying the need for reform and change.

title.narrative: 2. National and international support mobilized for efficient pricing and taxation of fossil fuels.
Contribution made to efficient pricing and fossil fuel taxation in at least two emerging economies.

target.value: Significantly increased international engagement on the potential of efficient fossil fuel pricing and use of taxation as a tool to support sustainable energy. Increased fossil fuel taxation promoted in 3 emerging economies, including possible Swaps.
